subject: zoology
question_text: Describe the three types of cartilage.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.33, SAQ 20). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK WORDING: the book writes that cartilage has 'chondroblasts enclosed in lacunae'. Chondroblasts are the young dividing cells; the cells lying in the lacunae of mature cartilage are chondrocytes, and the card uses chondrocytes.

steps.label: Cartilage
steps.why: Cartilage has no blood vessels inside it, so every fact about how it grows and how it repairs follows from the perichondrium lying on its surface.
common_mistakes: Writing that cartilage has its own blood supply. It has none; the perichondrium supplies it.
Calling the cells osteocytes. Bone has osteocytes; cartilage has chondrocytes.
steps.memory_tip: No blood inside cartilage — everything it needs comes from the perichondrium on the outside.
steps.margin_note: Definition, cells, lacunae, perichondrium, no blood supply. This is one mark, so keep the lines short.

steps.label: Hyaline cartilage
steps.why: Hyaline is the plain form with only fine collagen fibres, which is why it is both the weakest and the one found in the largest number of places.
common_mistakes: Calling hyaline cartilage the strongest. It is the weakest; fibrous cartilage is the strongest.
Giving the pinna as an example. The pinna is elastic cartilage.
steps.memory_tip: Hyaline means glassy: bluish white, see-through, weakest, and found almost everywhere.
steps.margin_note: Colour, fibres, strength, examples. Four short lines for each type.
lines: It is bluish white and translucent.
It is the weakest and the commonest cartilage.

steps.label: Elastic cartilage
steps.why: The extra elastic fibres are the only difference from hyaline, and they account for both the yellow colour and the springiness of the ear.
common_mistakes: Leaving out collagen. Elastic cartilage has elastic fibres IN ADDITION to collagen fibres.
Giving the intervertebral disc as an example. That is fibrous cartilage.
steps.memory_tip: Bend the ear and let it go: that is elastic cartilage, yellow and springy.
steps.margin_note: The same four points in the same order as hyaline. The examiner reads the pattern.

steps.label: Fibrous cartilage
steps.why: Thick collagen bundles make it the strongest, and it is the one type with no perichondrium, so both facts are asked again and again in short-answer papers.
common_mistakes: Writing that fibrous cartilage has a perichondrium. It is the only type without one.
Calling it the commonest. It is the strongest; hyaline is the commonest.
steps.memory_tip: Fibrous means fibre bundles, so it is the strongest — and the only one with no perichondrium.
steps.margin_note: Strength and the missing perichondrium are the two marked facts here.
